title: Downing provides £18.4m for Hertfordshire heritage scheme
summary:
Downing has provided £18.4 million in development finance to a regional developer for the conversion of the former Princess Helena College at Temple Dinsley in Preston, Hertfordshire, into 40 apartments and three houses. The financing will support the restoration of the Grade II* listed main building alongside the construction of 24 new-build homes.

title: Property industry seeks clarity ahead of Autumn Budget
summary:
Estate agents, landlords, housebuilders and mortgage specialists have called on Chancellor John Healey to provide greater certainty in the housing market ahead of today's Autumn Budget statement. Industry bodies across the property sector have submitted requests for policy clarity and tax reform, with consistent emphasis on reducing barriers to investment.

title: Estate agencies urged to prioritise first-party data
summary:
Estate agencies are being encouraged to shift their focus towards building first-party data assets as reliance on third-party platforms becomes increasingly costly and vulnerable to external changes. First-party data refers to information collected directly from customers, contrasting with data accessed through external platforms which agencies pay to use but do not own.

title: Fylde Coast group acquires agency despite ban history
summary:
Fylde Coast Homes Group has acquired Stephen Tew Estate Agents in Blackpool, with the founder remaining as head of sales and operations two years after receiving an 11-year director disqualification. The agency will retain its name and branding as part of the group's expansion strategy across the Fylde Coast region.

title: BestAgent launches membership club for estate agents
summary:
BestAgent is launching a membership organisation for estate agents in November, with entry based on assessed performance criteria rather than payment alone. The club will be limited to 1,000 members initially, with 99 founder memberships available at launch.

title: Estate agents support regulation to tackle rogue operators
summary:
A survey of 537 estate agents across England and Wales has revealed overwhelming support for increased government regulation of the property sector, with 92% backing plans for mandatory licensing and professional qualifications. The research found that 48% of agents reported encountering rogue or substandard agencies operating within their local markets.

title: Buy-to-let losses rise 32% to exceed £1 billion
summary:
Buy-to-let investors reported losses of £1.15 billion on property sales in the past year, a 32% increase from £870 million previously. The data from HMRC Capital Gains Tax returns reflects mounting pressure on landlords as property prices stagnate and regulatory burdens increase.

title: Lender provides full purchase price on below market value deal
summary:
District & County Investments has provided £370,000 in bridging finance to fund the full purchase price of a four-bedroom detached property in Luton acquired below market value. The lender assessed the facility against the property's market value rather than the discounted purchase price.

title: Atom bank provides £6.1m for Welsh farm diversification
summary:
Atom bank has provided a £6.12 million commercial loan to a South Wales farm business that has transitioned from dairy farming into hospitality and leisure operations. The enterprise now employs 100 people and operates glamping accommodation, a bistro, play facilities, and an event venue.

title: £35.5m build-to-rent finance backs Earlsfield scheme
summary:
United Trust Bank has provided £35.5m in build-to-rent finance for a 96-apartment mixed-use development in Earlsfield, south-west London. The facility allows developer Dominus New Homes to refinance its existing development loan as the scheme approaches practical completion.
